purpose: Represent one shared movable screen and three conceptual optical models with explicit ray recomputation.
assumptions: The three eyes are conceptual optical models, not three anatomical eyes.
The thin-lens model uses paraxial ray slopes and is illustrative; it does not represent a clinical prescription.
The screen is flat in this first prototype and can move in x, y and z.
The retina receives an inverted optical image before a conceptual perceptual reconstruction.
The axial object distance is used for the paraxial lens equation; exact 3D screen-to-eye distances are shown separately.
kill_tests: If screen movement does not alter all three ray bundles, reject the shared-screen implementation.
If aperture rays do not meet at the same calculated paraxial focus, reject the ray-slope implementation.
If the astigmatism model has only one image distance across its two meridians, reject the two-meridian implementation.
Do not infer a person’s refractive error or visual health from this sketch.
unknowns: How a real user perceives the alignment of the screen model.
Whether a future perceptual calibration improves comfort or task performance.
How curved and independently angled monitors should be represented in the production geometry.
